correctness.rationale: The canonical edge-difference map sends basepoint-zero real or complex Lipschitz functions on the cycle isometrically to H={b in K^n:sum b_i=0}, norm ||b||_infty; all graph metric inequalities follow from edge bounds. Averaging any positive quadratic/Hermitian form satisfying N²<=Q<=D²N² over coordinate permutations makes Q=c sum|b|² on H without increasing distortion; this is a globally optimal ellipsoid argument, not an unsupported diagonal restriction. Under max|b|=1, Cauchy–Schwarz gives min sum|b|²=n/(n-1), achieved by (1,-1/(n-1),...). On real cube section the convex square sum reaches its maximum at a vertex with at least n-1 saturated signs, yielding n for even n or n-1 with one zero coordinate for odd n. In complex case n-th roots of unity achieve all n unit-modulus coordinates with zero sum, so max=n. Hence squared distances are exactly the max/min ratios. Independently enumerated real cube-section vertices n=3..7 with rational extremum witnesses; finite computations do not prove general n.
